findings.evidence: template/scripts/lifecycle_workers.py provider_readiness: `str(result.get("limitation") or f"{provider} runtime is not ready")`. template/scripts/pr_review_gate.py complete_review: `next((... report.get("limitation") ...), "no reviewer report was produced")`. Both are new in this diff.
findings.summary: New code substitutes a generic message when the provider gives no limitation, hiding that the probe or report carried no diagnosis. The global no-fallback rule asks for an explicit failure or report instead of a default.

findings.evidence: lifecycle_workers.execute_job: `limitation = runtime_check() if runtime_check is not None else None`. run_claimed passes `runtime_check=repair_runtime_check if kind == "repair" else None`. main only builds `repair_runtime_check` when `args.repair_provider` is set. That is enforced for `--run` in the CLI, but not for other callers of run_claimed.
findings.summary: A repair writer failure is reclassified as unavailable only when `runtime_check` is supplied. `execute_job` silently keeps the old `failed` path when it is None, so any caller that omits the probe gets escalation instead of the retryable state without any signal.
